limits: The native partial pair measured c7ba6f593cb9d1435301cb79897331cc2f42a9d16ed39c84cb239c44d5608d27, before the shared full-mode ports; final 06c0 adapter has separate final browser acceptance and matched browser timings.
Native baseline has four populated page nodes in two sample starts and five in others; physical viewport/page/scale/offset and visible ink match. Do not claim identical full DOM state.

Native median workload wall time rose 2518→2800ms and rescale synchronous wall span 288→692ms. Lower p95 gaps are smoother frame delivery, not reduced total work/CPU. Nested synchronous spans are inclusive and must not be summed.
Full browser per-sample p95 ranges overlap substantially; 199.9→183.3ms is a modest local result, not a statistical guarantee.
Exact white background/black ink workload. Dark/tinted/inverted palette correctness verified separately; these timings do not predict their performance.
Browser and WebKit differ in event scheduling and device scale; do not compare absolute timings across engines.
Earlier browser measurements used an async Playwright wait predicate that did not actually poll; only the final94320b probe pair is selected here.
Standalone snapshots do not establish composed editor appearance. The subsequent default-promotion native journey passed in run-nxohoeg1; earlier failed/unavailable attempts remain in the audit.

Selected browser timing pairs use probe94320b with matching final physical start-state assertions; it validated only the second stability observation as rendered. Final test-only probe de605d validates both observations, including viewport size; its full/partial acceptance passed separately. The old samples do not prove this stronger first-observation contract.
